Q: Pins seem to be involved in the conflict. Currently pinned specs: - python 3.12.* (labeled as 'pin-1') A: 
conda install python=3.13 jupyter

Install the previous version of python that the problem was pinned on; e.g., if it was pinned on python=3.14, then install python 3.13.

Q: How to call the "Sound Setting" via command line in Windows A:

I wrote a standalone executable in Python that allows full control of Windows audio settings via the command line. In addition, it includes a GUI that interfaces with the Windows audio system using its own command-line backend.

The tool also features a learning function: if there’s an audio setting you want to toggle—whether from another program or through the command line—it can learn that action and expose it as a reusable command-line command for future use.
https://github.com/Mr5niper/WindowsAudioControl-CLI-wGUI

Q: CMake stdlib include issue A:

This is because target_link_libraries() will automatically include lib's include directories with -isystem, if the lib included system include dir, then include search order will be incorrect.

Firstly, include search order is important, because #include_next will actually include the file with the the same name BEHIND the current file(the file which use #include_next)'s include path, if there is no such a header, then compiler error occurs. Use -v flag in g++ to view the include search order, for example(incorrect one)

#include "..." search starts here:
#include <...> search starts here:
 D:/your_target/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0/x86_64-w64-mingw32
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0/backward
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/include-fixed
End of search list.

Pay attention to "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include" and "C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0", the first path is system include of C, while the second path is for C++. In this example, C include path is BEFORE C++ include path, and #include_next<stdlib.h> is happened in C++ include path(in header cstdlib), so compiler cannot find C version stdlib.h after"C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0" , because the #include_next target file is in C include path "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include". The correct search order is(and this is also the implicit order)

#include "..." search starts here:
#include <...> search starts here:
 D:/your_target/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0/x86_64-w64-mingw32
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/../../../../include/c++/15.2.0/backward
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/include
 C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-w64-mingw32/15.2.0/include-fixed
End of search list.

Unfortunately, we can't change the behavior of target_link_libraries(), if the lib has include directory "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include", then target_link_libraries() will generate -isystem "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include" in compiler flag(stored in includes_CXX.rsp), and this makes C include path before C++ include path(here C include is -isystem explicit, C++ include is implicit, behind all explicit -isystem flags).

The only way I know is to explicitly pass C and C++ system include with -isystem in correct order to your target, the following code works fine, but you have to find out C++ include path and C include path by your own(or hard-coded them in .cmake file).

target_include_directories(your_target SYSTEM PRIVATE "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include/c++/15.2.0" "C:/msys64/ucrt64/include")

I got these path in a general way, by using get_filename_component(root_path "${compiler_bin_dir}/.." ABSOLUTE)to get environment root path "C:/msys64/ucrt64", then use file(GLOB_RECURSE stdlib_paths "${root_path}/stdlib.h") to search stdlib.h in root_path. The result list stdlib_paths has both C and C++ stdlib.h, in my case the first is C++ include and the last is C include.

Q: npm run fails because IntelliJ can't find npm even though it is installed A:

I ran into this problem with PhpStorm, and I think it may have been caused by me

  1. installing Node 20 via NVM

  2. setting up the IDE

  3. switching to Node 24 in NVM as the default version

  4. removing Node 24 in NVM

In Settings > Languages & Frameworks > JavaScript Runtime > Node runtime, I saw that it was still pointing at the Node 20 path. I switched it to the correct Node 24 path, and that solved the problem.

Q: Change Published Calendar TimeZone in AWS Connect A:

You cannot change the timezone of a Published Calendar in Amazon Connect.
Once a calendar is published, its timezone is locked permanently.

Q: Expo development build failing: Error resolving plugin [id: 'com.facebook.react.settings'] (React Native 0.76.9, SDK 52) A:

Irmão, sei que ninguém respondeu e já tem anos, mas se alguém acabar caindo aqui novamente, vai a resposta

Exclua a pasta:

C:\Users\seu-usuario\.gradle

Em seguida, faça o build novamente e tente rodar o projeto.

Isso normalmente resolve problemas causados por cache corrompido ou desatualizado do Gradle.
